hero.title: Creator & Host
hero.intro: Seven questions carefully crafted. One half question from AI. One conversation you couldn't have planned.

paragraphs.text: A lifetime New Yorker with duel USA and German citzenship, Priscilla Beaton has always been drawn to compelling people, original ideas, and the stories behind what people create.

Her distinctly New York education began in the twos program at the Barnard College Center for Toddler Development, where she learned an early lesson that stayed with her: when something matters, hold on tighter if you don't want to loose it! As the youngest of four children and the only girl among three brothers learning to speak up, stand her ground, and think independently began early.

Priscilla went on to attend the Episcopal School in the City of New York, where an imaginative approach to storytellin filled with literature, music, rhythm, humor, and stories created by the children themselves—helped awaken her earliest love of narrative. That foundation continued through eleven formative years at the Spence School, where a rigorous emphasis on writing sharpened her skills and deepened her interest in the stories people have to tell. She later attended the Professional Children's School which enabled her to move to Los Angeles and intern for MGM Unscipted. The schools  individualized and a faculty that encouraged students to follow their passion from a young age showed her how the right support can help young people pursue ambitious goals while continuing to grow academically and creatively. This opportunity is a big part of what has shaped the mentor part of Seven and Half, the belief that every person

She earned her undergraduate degree from Barnard College, Columbia University, and later completed her master's degree at Columbia University's Graduate School of Journalism. Her professional experience spans writing, script development, television production, and creative strategy. She also helped found and served as creative director of Snack Bowery, a pop-up snack shop and art gallery that brought together emerging artists, creativity, and community.

A lifelong advocate for animals, Priscilla is particularly devoted to Felix, her family's rescue dog and the inspiration for a short story she is writing about his unlikely friendship and nighttime playdates with the coyotes of Central Park. Giving back to animal charities is an important part of her vision for Seven and a Half—and a reflection of her belief that storytelling can create connection, inspire compassion, and reach far beyond the page.

Together, these experiences inspired Seven and a Half: an editorial platform and mentoring community created to spark curiosity, encourage authentic conversation, and help people of all ages develop their talents and thrive.

At the heart of its mentoring community is a simple idea: one person and one conversation can change the course of a life. It might happen over dinner, in a coffee shop, or while standing beside someone in line. The online world extends that possibility, connecting people with mentors they might never otherwise meet—people whose experience can offer a new perspective, a thoughtful answer, or the piece of advice that changes what comes next.

Built on Priscilla's belief that the best conversations begin where the predictable questions end, Seven and a Half invites fascinating people to share the stories that rarely surface in a traditional interview—because sometimes half a question can reveal more than a whole one.

halfQuestion.label: The Half Question
halfQuestion.heading: Why AI writes the last question
halfQuestion.body: At the end of every interview, an AI reads the full transcript and generates a single question — one that couldn't have been written in advance, because it emerges from the specific conversation that just happened. It is entirely out of Priscilla's hands. Unexpected, unpredictable, and entirely its own.
halfQuestion.pullQuote: A question neither of us knew was coming.

connect.label: Get in touch
connect.heading: Pitch a guest or just say hello
connect.body: The best conversations come from unexpected suggestions. If you know someone who should answer the half question, Priscilla wants to hear about it.
